message.content: {"ranking": [{"id": "patch_b9cc3bb103f8", "failure_port": "o_mosi", "source_line": 278, "mechanism": "The gating condition for the command state machine transition (`pre_cmd_state`) is currently only qualified by `!ll_cmd_stb`. In the failing trace, `pre_cmd_state` erroneously asserts on cycle 484124 while `ll_cmd_stb` remains high, causing the state machine to advance `r_cmd_state` prematurely. This shifts the byte stream driven onto `ll_cmd_dat` and subsequently serialized onto `o_mosi` by exactly one cycle, producing the observed alternating 0/1 mismatches at cycles 484124-484127. Adding `pre_cmd_state` to the gate ensures the state machine only advances when the low-level interface is truly idle."}, {"id": "patch_3e6c1ef8f5ff", "failure_port": "o_mosi", "source_line": 22110, "mechanism": "The FIFO write lanes for both FIFO A and FIFO B consume `wb_data` with identical byte ordering. The current implementation writes `wb_data` directly into the byte-wide memories without byte-reversal, but the Wishbone bus is little-endian while the SD SPI protocol expects big-endian byte order on the wire. The bundle patch reverses the byte lanes for both FIFO A (line 22110) and FIFO B (line 23064) simultaneously, correcting the byte stream fed to the low-level transmitter and aligning the serialized `o_mosi` bits with the reference trace from cycle 484128 onward."}, {"id": "patch_55de7eef4688", "failure_port": "o_mosi", "source_line": 337, "mechanism": "At `r_cmd_state == 3'h6` the state machine decides whether to continue FIFO read transactions by checking `r_use_fifo` alone. When `r_use_fifo` is asserted but the low-level FIFO read has not actually been armed (`ll_fifo_rd` low), the state machine still advances and drives `ll_cmd_dat` with `8'hff`/`fifo_byte` one cycle early. This prematurely changes the MOSI bitstream. Qualifying the transition with `r_use_fifo` (which reflects the armed read intent) keeps the state machine stalled until the low-level read channel is active, eliminating the early `o_mosi` transitions at cycles 484124-484127."}, {"id": "patch_0ce0a636b1ee", "failure_port": "o_mosi", "source_line": 334, "mechanism": "The condition enabling `ll_fifo_rd` and the associated `ll_cmd_dat` load at `r_cmd_state == 3'h5` is gated only by `(r_use_fifo)&&(r_fifo_wr)`. In the failing run, `r_fifo_wr` asserts before `ll_fifo_rd_complete` returns, so the state machine enters the FIFO-read branch and starts emitting `fifo_byte` onto `ll_cmd_dat` (and thus `o_mosi`) while the low-level read pipeline is still filling. Adding `ll_fifo_rd_complete` to the gate holds the state machine in the `8'hff` padding state until the read pipeline signals completion, preventing the early data-phase MOSI edges observed at cycles 484124-484127."}, {"id": "patch_3fe26dfae867", "failure_port": "o_mosi", "source_line": 324, "mechanism": "The branch at `r_cmd_state == 3'h5` that sets `r_cmd_state <= r_cmd_state + 3'h2` (skipping FIFO read) is taken whenever `r_have_resp` is true and `r_use_fifo` is false. In the trace, `r_have_resp` asserts one cycle before the low-level interface has actually returned the response token, so the state machine jumps to the post-command `8'hff` phase early. Qualifying the `r_have_resp` check with the FIFO-read intent (`r_use_fifo`) ensures the non-FIFO fast-path is only taken when a FIFO read is not pending, delaying the state advance until the true response arrives and fixing the early `o_mosi` transitions."}, {"id": "patch_171aea9942d8", "failure_port": "o_mosi", "source_line": 334, "mechanism": "The FIFO write enable (`ll_fifo_wr`) is armed when `(r_use_fifo)&&(r_fifo_wr)` becomes true at `r_cmd_state == 3'h5`. However, `r_have_resp` can assert before the low-level command/response handshake finishes, causing `ll_fifo_wr` to assert while `ll_idle` is still low. The patch adds `r_have_resp` to the FIFO-write gate, ensuring the write channel only opens after the command response has been received, which aligns the first `ll_cmd_dat`/`o_mosi` payload cycle with the reference at cycle 484128."}, {"id": "patch_2e6db5d7770e", "failure_port": "o_mosi", "source_line": 300, "mechanism": "The very first state transition (`r_cmd_state == 3'h0` -> `3'h1`) is currently unconditional once `pre_cmd_state` asserts. In the failing trace, `pre_cmd_state` pulses high while `ll_cmd_stb` is still asserted from the previous command, so the state machine emits the first command byte (`r_data_reg[31:24]`) one cycle early. Adding `!ll_cmd_stb` to the gate forces the state machine to wait until the low-level transmitter has fully returned to idle, eliminating the leading MOSI mismatch at cycle 484124."}, {"id": "patch_f98cd079ac46", "failure_port": "o_mosi", "source_line": 327, "mechanism": "At `r_cmd_state == 3'h4` the state machine loads the CRC byte and decides whether to enter the FIFO-read wait state (`3'h5`) or the non-FIFO response wait state. The current gate uses `r_have_resp` alone, but `r_have_resp` can be set by the non-FIFO response path while a FIFO read is actually pending (`r_use_fifo` high). The patch adds `!r_use_fifo` so the non-FIFO branch is only taken when no FIFO read is configured, preventing the state machine from skipping the FIFO-read setup and emitting `8'hff` padding instead of the start-token `8'hfe`, which corrects the MOSI stream from cycle 484124."}], "explanation": "The public failure shows a burst of MOSI bit errors starting at cycle 484124, exactly when a new command is accepted (`new_cmd` high) and the command state machine begins transmitting bytes. All top-ranked patches target the gating conditions that control the command state machine (`r_cmd_state`) and the low-level command strobe (`ll_cmd_stb`). Each patch adds a missing qualifier (idle flags, FIFO completion, FIFO intent, or CRC-path selection) that prevents the state machine from advancing one cycle too early. Advancing early shifts the entire MOSI bitstream by one cycle, producing the alternating 0/1 mismatches seen at cycles 484124-484127 and the subsequent payload misalignment from cycle 484128 onward. The FIFO byte-order bundle (`patch_3e6c1ef8f5ff`) addresses a separate but co-occurring byte-endian mismatch that would corrupt the payload bytes once the timing is fixed. Together, these eight patches cover the three root causes: premature state-machine launch, incorrect FIFO-read/write gating, and Wishbone-to-SPI byte-order reversal."}
